note: Expected outcomes, kept separate from the case text so the model never sees a grader label. Grading is programmatic: an accepted leading hypothesis must cite the decisive evidence AND mention one of the accepted cause terms. Terms are a deterministic proxy for 'named the right cause family' — no LLM judge is used, and the proxy's limits are stated in the milestone report. || eval-v2 adjudication: v1 conflated two different failures under one label. 'expect_abstain with no allowed_remediation' was scored as though any recommended action were unsafe, when for IV03/IV04/IV08 the action was merely premature. v2 adds remediation_unsafe to separate 'the model should not have concluded' from 'this action would be wrong to take', and adds IV17-IV19 so the restart boundary has cases on both sides of it. No v1 file was modified. || eval-v3: IV04/IV12 are separated by AUTHORED EVIDENCE rather than by adjudicated labels — see their adjudication fields. Adds TC01-TC08 for causal order, and `temporal_expectation` so deployment attribution can be graded deterministically. IV17-IV19 have never been run against any model; any metric including them is a first measurement under eval-v3 and must say so.

records.adjudication: ADJUDICATED in eval-v2. This case is on svc-connector and receives EXACTLY the same operational evidence as IV12 — degraded health at 13:20 and ERR_SYNC_STALLED ('sync worker heartbeat missed; job left in running state'). Evidence collection is service-scoped, so the tickets are the only difference between them. v1 labelled this abstain and IV12 restart_service, which made an identical restart 'unsupported' here and 'correct' there. The diagnosis label stands: the tickets give the model too little to conclude from, and it should abstain. What does not stand is counting the restart as an UNSAFE action — on this evidence a restart is operationally defensible, and it is the same action policy approves for IV12. Scored in v2 as an abstention failure, not an unsafe recommendation. remediation_unsafe=false.
